admission.justification: Future cancellation and retained-state refactors must preserve the two-holder boundary: returning to index-only classification strands staged deletions and tempts manual loss-prone recovery.

alternatives.option: Require successful absence from both index and current HEAD, and preserve tracked deletions through native patches.
alternatives.reason: It retains the patch/mirror boundary while allowing the product to cancel the observed stopped sync without losing the parked partition or later genuine untracked bytes.

alternatives.option: Treat absence from the index alone as untracked and attempt a file mirror.
alternatives.reason: A staged deletion is absent from the index but still HEAD-tracked; a nonexistent-file mirror refuses even though staged.patch already carries the deletion. This is the rejected prior implementation boundary, not a claim that a design meeting considered it.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if Git holder or save-format semantics change so that every staged deletion is independently representable and cancellation preserves its index/worktree partition without a nonexistent-file mirror.

consequences: Retain successful Git inspection as the absence precondition; read errors do not authorize mirroring.
Preserve the shared classifier for save-first cancellation and retained fingerprints rather than adding a bypass or second classifier.
context: Index absence is not proof of untracked state: a staged deletion is still held by HEAD and the native staged patch. The observed old classifier sent it to a nonexistent-file mirror, preventing product cancellation.
decider: Architect successor ruling of 2026-10-15 under unchanged MIK-R61@v1 rule12 and developer D253.

evidence: Architect successor ruling, canonical S8, Worker stop-inventory-successor.md and Reviewer L61-round9-rule12-verdict.md: former index-only classification stranded staged-deletion cancellation.
